claims.text: Multi-replica parallel tempering combined with well-tempered metadynamics can accurately determine melting properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Collective variables based on atomic coordination and order are sufficient to capture melting in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method can determine melting temperature.
The proposed method can determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
The proposed method can determine volume change at melting.
The proposed method can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Replicas will be distributed over an interval of approximately 0.8Tm to 1.2Tm.
Simulations will use approximately 100 ns per replica.
Temperature spacings of 50–100 K will ensure sufficient sampling of phase transitions.
Atomic-scale order and disorder captured by the collective variables mediates the connection between enhanced sampling and the calculated thermodynamic properties.
High-entropy alloys have slow melting kinetics and free-energy barriers that impede conventional sampling.
The enhanced-sampling method accelerates phase-transition events by overcoming slow kinetics and free-energy barriers.
Biasing well-chosen order parameters enables efficient exploration of both solid and liquid states.
Exploration of both solid and liquid states enables convergence of melting properties that would otherwise be computationally prohibitive or inaccurate.
The approach will be more efficient than conventional methods.
Conventional calorimetry, empirical or semi-empirical models, and first-principles calculations struggle with accuracy or computational cost across the diverse HEA composition space.
The method applies to high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures.
Systems with extreme compositional or phase complexity may require additional calibration.
Prior evidence in simpler alloy systems supports the effectiveness of the proposed enhanced-sampling approach.
Extrapolation to the full HEA family is uncertain because optimal collective variables and biasing parameters may vary among systems.
